summary.text: Steve Womack is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 3rd District, seeking re-election. A retired Arkansas Army National Guard colonel and former mayor of Rogers, he was first elected to the House in 2010 and sits on the Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Womack graduated from Arkansas Tech University with a bachelor's degree in 1979 and was inducted into the university's Hall of Distinction in 2014.

He served in the Arkansas Army National Guard from 1979 to 2009 and retired as a colonel with more than thirty years of service. His 2002 deployment to the Sinai in Egypt was the first time a National Guard unit performed the Multinational Force and Observers mission.
His military awards include the Legion of Merit, the Arkansas Distinguished Service Medal and, in 2015, the National Guard Bureau's Harry S. Truman Award.
Before entering elected office, Womack worked as a radio station manager and consultant. He served on the Rogers City Council (1983-1984 and 1997-1998), then as mayor of Rogers from 1999 to 2010.
He won election to the U.S. House in 2010 and has represented Arkansas's 3rd District since.

Womack is a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, chairing its Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Subcommittee and sitting on the Defense and Financial Services and General Government subcommittees; he previously chaired the House Budget Committee.
In 2018 he led the bipartisan, bicameral Joint Select Committee on Budget and Appropriations Process Reform, and he has served as chairman of the West Point Board of Visitors since 2017.
According to his House biography, he lives in Rogers and is the father of three sons.
